items.title: Why don’t I have Siri AI on my iPhone?
items.content_html:
Macworld

Apple’s Siri voice assistant was famously bad for a long time, but the company turned a corner with the launch of Siri AI, an upgraded assistant powered by the latest generation of Apple Intelligence with better accuracy and more features. Siri AI was announced at WWDC in June 2026 and arrived with iOS 27 on September 14. But it isn’t immediately available to everyone: access depends on your iPhone model, software version, language, Apple Account region, and a temporary waiting list.

So how do you actually get it? Siri AI doesn’t simply appear on your iPhone; you’ll need to clear a few hurdles before you can turn it on. In this brief tutorial, we explain what might be holding things up and show you how to get Siri AI on your iPhone.

Install iOS 27

First, update your iPhone to iOS 27 if you haven’t already. Open the Settings app and go to General > Software Update, then wait while your iPhone checks for available updates. If you see multiple options, select the latest iOS 27 version and follow the onscreen instructions to download and install it.

Your iPhone will restart when the update is complete.

Make sure you have enough storage

Siri AI and the latest Apple Intelligence features require lots of space. Depending on your iPhone, Apple says you may need up to 14GB of available storage.

To check, go to Settings > General > iPhone Storage. If you’re running short, you’ll need to free up some space before Siri AI can finish downloading. See: How to save space on an iPhone.

Check if Siri is available in your Apple Account region

Has Apple made Siri AI available in your country yet?

If your Apple Account is registered in the European Union, you’re mostly out of luck. Apple has delayed the launch of Siri AI for iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch in the EU, claiming that it needs more time to comply with the Digital Markets Act. The EU disputes Apple’s interpretation of the law. There is some hope that the situation may change. In the meantime, EU users can access Siri AI on a compatible Mac or Apple Vision Pro.

Users in mainland China also miss out on Siri AI while, in Tim Cook’s words, “Apple works through regulatory requirements.”

Set the device and Siri languages correctly

Siri AI currently supports English only. Wherever you are, you’ll need to have your device language and Siri language both set to English.

Once Siri AI has been activated, it will continue working even if you travel to a region where it isn’t available. Eligibility depends on your Apple Account region and device, rather than simply your location.

Check your iPhone model: Is your iPhone (or other Apple device) compatible with Siri AI?

The next step is to make sure your iPhone is compatible with Siri AI, which makes substantial demands on the processor and therefore won’t run on older and slower hardware.

Siri AI supports the iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max, every iPhone 16 model and later, and iPhone Air.

Here’s a list of currently available iPhones that can run Siri AI. Any phones that Apple launches in the future will also be compatible.

  • iPhone Duo
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • iPhone 18 Pro
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max
  • iPhone 17 Pro
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone 17
  • iPhone 17e
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16 Pro
  • iPhone 16 Plus
  • iPhone 16
  • iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 15 Pro

If you’re unsure which iPhone model you’ve got, open the Settings app and go to General > About then look for Model Name in the top box.

Is your iPhone on the list? Great! There are just a couple more steps to take. (Plus potentially a bit of a wait.)

Siri AI is also available on the following Apple devices:

  • iPad mini (A17 Pro) or any iPad model with M1 or later running iPadOS 27
  • MacBook Neo (A18 Pro) or any Mac with M1 or later running macOS 27 Golden Gate
  • Apple Watch Series 9 or later, Apple Watch Ultra 2 or later, or Apple Watch SE 3, running watchOS 27 and paired with Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone
  • Any Apple Vision Pro running visionOS 27

For more detail, read our article listing all Siri AI-compatible devices.

Turn on Siri and join the waiting list

Foundry

Open the Settings app and tap Siri. If Siri is currently turned off, enable it before continuing. At the top of the screen, tap Try Siri AI (Beta), then follow the onscreen instructions to choose a voice, complete voice enrollment, and review the privacy settings.

Once setup is complete, you’ll be added to Apple’s waiting list and the status will change to Joined Waiting List.

Now you wait. Some iPhone owners have gained access within minutes, while others have waited for hours or days. Wait times vary, but Siri AI will download automatically when access is granted. You’ll receive a notification when it’s ready to use.

Then you can start exploring the first truly capable version of Siri in years and all sorts of cool new features. Have fun.

items.title: Danny MacAskill Plays in the Endless Light of Norway
items.content_html:
Scottish trials rider and mountain biker Danny MacAskill, who I first featured on the site more than 17 years ago, recently took his Santa Cruz eMTB north of the Arctic Circle to Narvik, Norway. He rode three different mountains and the result is this incredibly beautiful video, backed by a Max Cooper soundtrack. As one of the commenters notes, MacAskill makes a relatively heavy eMTB seem extraordinarily playful.

As a mountain biker myself, some of that looks insanely fun but the narrow steep stuff looks insanely insane. Makes me want an eMTB, which I suppose is the whole point of the video.
